original_question: Are either of the Borel-cover properties S_1(B_Ω, B_Ω) or S_fin(B_Ω, B_Ω) hereditary, meaning that every subspace of a space with the property must also have the property?
target_in_paper: Section 8.1, Problem 5: "Is any of the properties S_1(B_Ω, B_Ω) or S_fin(B_Ω, B_Ω) hereditary?"
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the exact two Borel-cover properties named in the paper and the correct preservation issue: hereditariness under passing to subsets/subspaces. In the paper's default setting of sets of reals, your use of "subspace" is essentially the same as the paper's "subset" formulation.
missing_details: The official formulation is an open problem in Section 8.1, labeled Problem 5.
The paper's default scope is spaces homeomorphic to sets of reals (equivalently, in particular, separable zero-dimensional metrizable spaces), unless otherwise indicated.
B_Ω denotes the family of countable Borel ω-covers of the space.
A cover is assumed to be nontrivial: X = ⋃𝒰 and X ∉ 𝒰.
An ω-cover means that every finite subset of X is contained in some member of the cover.
S_1(B_Ω, B_Ω) means: for every sequence (𝒰_n) of members of B_Ω(X), one can choose U_n ∈ 𝒰_n so that {U_n : n ∈ ℕ} is again in B_Ω(X).
S_fin(B_Ω, B_Ω) means: for every sequence (𝒰_n) of members of B_Ω(X), one can choose finite 𝔽_n ⊆ 𝒰_n so that ⋃_n 𝔽_n is in B_Ω(X).
Hereditary is defined in the paper as: whenever X has the property, every subset Y ⊆ X also has it, with the induced topology and the corresponding relative Borel ω-covers.
Your wording "Are either of ... hereditary" is slightly ambiguous; the paper's wording asks whether at least one of the two listed properties is hereditary.
The paper notes a nearby but different finite-power question (Problem 7) whose positive solution would imply a positive answer here, but it is not presented as an equivalent reformulation.
refined_question: For a space X in the paper’s default setting (typically a set of reals), let B_Ω(X) be the family of countable Borel ω-covers of X, where a cover 𝒰 is nontrivial (X = ⋃𝒰 and X ∉ 𝒰) and every finite subset of X is contained in some U ∈ 𝒰. Is at least one of the two selection properties S_1(B_Ω, B_Ω) or S_fin(B_Ω, B_Ω) hereditary; that is, if X satisfies one of these properties, must every subset Y ⊆ X, with the induced topology and its own family B_Ω(Y) of countable Borel ω-covers, satisfy the same property?
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 8.1 on hereditariness, and in fact matches Problem 5 almost verbatim. To make it fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must unpack the notation S_1 and S_fin from Section 2.1, the meaning of ω-cover and B_Ω from Sections 2.3 and 3, and the paper's definition of hereditary as closure under passing to all subsets. The neighboring finite-power question in Section 8.2 is only stated as related and implication-bearing, not as an equivalent replacement, so the refined question should remain Problem 5 itself rather than drift to Problem 7.
